cases.name: canonical brisket — rain dip and a 1h50m stall

engine: A stall is detected inside the 150-170F band, starting within +/-20 min of stallStartUtcMillis and ending within +/-20 min of stallEndUtcMillis.
The pit rain dip to 221F at 11:05 AM is a pit event, never a stall signal: no stall may be reported before the probe enters the band.
A finish range stated from the last 30 minutes of readings at any point after the stall must contain finishUtcMillis (16:45).
Stall duration computes to 2h40m (+/-20 min at each end).
Total cook duration food_on to remove computes to 13h10m — the compare corpus anchor for the foil case.
The foil wrap at 11:20 falls inside the stall; the stall end is the probe's exit from the plateau, not the wrap.
No stall is reported: the probe crosses the 150-170F band still climbing at the end of the cook — presence in the band is not a stall without a sustained flat slope.
A pace range is available early (dense readings, steady slope) and contains finishUtcMillis.
The stall is detected even though the probe creeps 156->163F across it: in-band with slope under the floor for 5h is a stall, not progress.
Mid-stall, the finish range widens (or the basis reverts to the plan) rather than sliding the finish earlier on the creep's slope — the anti-jumpiness case.
The 03:00 pit dip to 228F does not end, restart, or split the stall.

cases.name: boston butt — hand-logged, six readings, no controller

engine: NO pace range is produced at any point: one food-probe reading cannot support a slope. The plan window is the only finish guidance, with the plan basis stated.
No stall is reported or ruled out: with no probe series, stall state is 'unknown', never 'no stall'.
The six hand readings are still first-class data: pit checks render as the cook's record (the S7-C card case) and the single 203F probe reading is the finish evidence.
